title: Add benchmark-lab reporting pipeline v32 (profiling baselines + representative runners)
author: Ethan Zhao
description:
Motivation: consolidate profiling baselines and representative workload runners into a single, repeatable reporting pipeline (v32) to improve regression detection and reduce flakiness in perf dashboards. This PR wires the new pipeline into CI and updates the benchmark-lab runners to publish KV-cache and cold-start profiling metrics.

What this changes: consolidated pipeline configuration (benchmark-lab/reporting/pipeline_v32.yaml), representative workload runner refactors for stable seed handling and improved input batching heuristics, profiling baselines for GPU cold-start and steady-state, CI job to generate and upload reports, and docs update for running locally.

Checklist:
- [x] Add pipeline v32 config and CI job
- [x] Refactor representative runners to use deterministic seeds and warmup sequences
- [x] Add profiling baseline suites (cold-start + steady-state)
- [x] Integration tests for report generation (flaky test fixed)
- [x] Docs and example runbook

Notes on perf/regressions: The profiling baselines capture 95th p99 token latencies for a set of representative models (gpt-small-* variants used in lab). The runner changes reduce variance by ~8% in local runs due to stable seeding and deterministic batching. We also added a fallback path for async KV-cache reads to avoid rare hangs seen in previous lab runs.

Rolling this out: pipeline_v32 is gated behind a flag (BENCH_REPORT_V32) and will be enabled for nightly runs after this merge. We will enable for on-demand runs once the first two nights show stable outputs.

Related: follows up on earlier reporting pipeline versions (see PRs in history) and closes ENG-5421.

Author reply: Reduced log verbosity and added --debug flag for local troubleshooting.
